records.real_world_identity_notes: The best-supported match is the Brazilian first-generation, pre-facelift Virtus 1.0 200 TSI from the 2018 launch specification. Reiza's official TSI Cup description pairs the plain Virtus entry with the project's separate 1.4 GTS specification; the independent Volkswagen technical sheet and launch coverage identify the plain 200 TSI Virtus as the 1.0 turbo sedan. This is distinct from the later Virtus GTS and from the India-market Virtus naming used for a different market range.
records.confidence_basis: The official Volkswagen technical sheet is dated January 2018 and identifies the Virtus 1.0 TSI automatic with its six-speed ratios and torque converter. Contemporary Brazilian coverage identifies the 2018 Virtus 200 TSI in Comfortline and Highline forms and documents its automatic Tiptronic/paddle interface. Reiza's official AMS2 announcement confirms that the TSI Cup contains both the Virtus 1.0 TSI and the separate 1.4 GTS specification; the observed plain telemetry name therefore aligns with the 1.0 200 TSI branch, while the GTS name is handled separately in issue #43.

records.specification_basis: The official technical sheet specifies six forward ratios and contemporary coverage confirms a six-speed automatic. The manufacturer sheet explicitly says automatic and specifies a torque converter; Quatro Rodas corroborates the automatic 200 TSI configuration. The launch equipment list and contemporary coverage document steering-wheel paddles for the automatic Virtus 200 TSI. The sources explicitly describe sequential changes using the automatic transmission's steering-wheel paddles. The exact 200 TSI Virtus uses an automatic torque-converter transmission; normal move-off is performed through the automatic selector, brake, and accelerator without driver clutch operation. Paddle upshifts operate the automatic transmission; the documented driver interface has no clutch operation. Paddle downshifts operate the automatic transmission; the documented driver interface has no clutch operation. The exact car has an automatic Tiptronic/paddle interface rather than a manual gearbox requiring a driver throttle blip on upshift. The exact car has an automatic Tiptronic/paddle interface rather than a manual gearbox requiring a driver throttle blip on downshift. The full-resolution 2018 Virtus Highline cockpit photograph shows a conventional continuous rim with a clearly flattened lower section, not fixed GT/formula grips. The photograph shows the digital instrument cluster behind the rim, and the written source places the display in the separate cluster rather than in the wheel. The full-resolution image shows the upper band of the conventional wheel intact; only the lower section is flattened. The clear cockpit photograph shows no dedicated shift/rev-light strip on the rim; the visible digital display is separate behind it. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
